quizzes.title: Week 1: TypeScript Fundamentals
quizzes.scope: The Basics, Everyday Types, Narrowing, More on Functions (through overloads), Object Types.
quizzes.scoring_note: Wrong answers on T/F and multiple choice are subtracted from right answers. Do not guess. Short answer questions are graded on correctness and conciseness — do not write more than is asked for.

questions.question: TypeScript is a statically typed superset of JavaScript: all valid JavaScript is valid TypeScript.
questions.explanation: TypeScript is a strict superset of JavaScript. Any valid JS file is valid TS (though it may produce type errors under strict settings).

questions.question: What is a fragment in React?
questions.model_answer: A fragment is a wrapper that allows you to group multiple elements without creating a new DOM node. This is needed because React components must return a single root element.

questions.question: What does the calc() function do in CSS?
questions.model_answer: The calc() function in CSS lets you perform math calculations directly in your styles, mixing different units together.

questions.question: What does the @NoArgsConstructor annotation do?
questions.model_answer: @NoArgsConstructor is a Lombok annotation that automatically generates a no-argument constructor for your class, saving you from writing boilerplate code.

questions.question: What does the @AllArgsConstructor annotation do?
questions.model_answer: @AllArgsConstructor is a Lombok annotation that generates a constructor with one parameter for every field in your class.

questions.question: What is a static variable in Java?
questions.model_answer: A static variable belongs to the class itself, not to any individual object. If every object shares the same value, make it static.

questions.question: What does the @Builder annotation do?
questions.model_answer: @Builder is a Lombok annotation that generates a builder pattern for your class, letting you construct objects with a clean, readable, step-by-step syntax.

questions.question: What is the inferred type of `value`?
questions.explanation: `let` with an array literal infers a general array type: `number[]`. A tuple would require `as const` or an explicit annotation.
